newsitem.title: DUBAI: Saudi Arabia's Ibn Rushd mandates $850 mln loan.
newsitem.headline: Saudi Arabia's Ibn Rushd mandates $850 mln loan.

text.p: Saudi Arabia's Industrial Fibres Company (Ibn Rushd) has mandated a consortium of eight regional and international banks to arrange a $850 million syndicated loan for its petrochemical projects, bankers said on Sunday.

They said the compnay, owned by the industrial and petrochemical giant Saudi Basic Industries Corp (SABIC) as well as Saudi and Bahraini firms, wants to use the loan for three projects in Saudi Arabia.

They said the banks participating in the arrangement are Riyadh-based Arab National Bank -- owned by Amman-based Arab Bank and Saudi investors -- Saudi Arabia's Riyad Bank, Bahrain-based Gulf International Bank, JP Morgan, Britian's Barclays Bank Plc, Industrial Bank of Japan, The Arab Petroleum Investments Corp (APICORP) and Saudi Cairo Bank.
"The eight banks are equal arrangers. The banks are waiting for a final mandate letter from Ibn Rushd and then will start putting the syndication together," one banker in the Gulf said.
Another banker said the consortium will approcah regional and international banks to take part in the syndication, the first mandated by Ibn Rushd.
The bankers did not foresee any problems in raising the loan since Ibn Rushd had a "good reputation" and was affiliated to SABIC, seen as having a strong financial performance.

"A good indication that there will be both regional and international interest in this syndication is that Ibn Rushd had only given a two-week deadline for banks to bid for the arrangement mandate and refused to extend the period. Even so, there was a lot of bids put in," one of the bankers said.
The bids had closed at the end of October and the mandate was given to the eight banks around 10 days ago, he added.

Ibn Rushd will use the loan to finance the construction of a 350,000-tonnes per year purified terephthalic acid (PTA) plant -- due to come on stream in 1997 -- as well as a world-scale aromatic plant -- which would produce 350,000 metric tonnes of benzene a year and 300,000 metric tonnes of paraxylene a year. It will also produce orthoxylene and metaxylene and is due to come on stream by early 1998.

"It will also use some of the money towards its polyester plant which it had used its own money to construct," one banker said. Ibn Rushd had opened the 140,000 tonnes a year plant, at a cost of six billion riyals ($1.6 billion), in June this year.
Saudi Arabia is expanding and opening up its petrochemical sector to private finance in an attempt to diversify its oil-dominated economy.
New multi-million dollar petrochemical plants feeding off the country's abundant gas reserves are expected to come on stream until early into the next decade.

The petrochemical industry is expected to grow at an annual average rate of 8.3 percent in the state's sixth five-year development plan (1995-2000), outpacing 3.8 percent growth in oil and natural gas sector, according to forecasts by the Saudi Planning Ministry.
